defect: Migration 0061 named iam_v2.p3_entitlement_data_usage as the authoritative derivation that consumed_data_bytes must equal. After the live crossing the two disagreed by exactly one sample - the crossing itself, 497,220 bytes: counter 100,108,666 against derived 99,611,446. The Entitlement terminated at the crossing sample's instant, so the Session's binding closed at that instant, and the attribution predicate is half-open (bound_until > sampled_at). The sample that ended the access fell outside the interval the moment the interval closed, and was attributed to nothing.
fix: Migration 0062, applied through the authoritative runner. A closing binding may claim a sample at its own closing instant ONLY when no other binding for that session covers that instant. THE HALF-OPEN BOUND IS UNCHANGED, because it is what makes a Phase-5 rebinding unambiguous: the predecessor closes at T, the successor opens at T, and a sample at T belongs to the successor alone. Widening the bound to >= would attribute that sample to both and invent usage out of a transfer. The new arm is unreachable wherever a successor covers the instant, so it fires only at a terminal boundary - where there is no successor - and a sample is still attributed EXACTLY ONCE. 0062 asserts both properties against the real data before it commits: every counter equals its derivation, and no accounting record attributes to two bindings.

No accounting, admission or financial semantics change. The maintained counter was already correct and was not rewritten; the derivation now agrees with it rather than the other way round.
